label: History
value: Anne was born in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia.
unit: Born in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia, Anne was orphaned early in life and endured an unhappy childhood as an unloved drudge before being taken in at Green Gables by Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert. In Avonlea, she attended school, formed an intense academic rivalry with Gilbert Blythe, and established deep friendships, notably with Diana Barry. She attended Queen's Academy, where she earned her First Class License and won the Avery scholarship, before returning home to teach in Avonlea and found the Avonlea Village Improvement Society. Anne later attended Redmond College alongside friends like Priscilla Grant and Philippa Gordon, earning her degree and winning the Thorburn Scholarship. After teaching in Summerside for three years, she married Gilbert Blythe in Green Gables and moved with him to their new home in Four Winds, later raising their children at Ingleside.

label: History
value: Anthony was taken in as an orphan nephew by Mrs. George Pye
unit: After being taken in as an orphan nephew by Mrs. George Pye and her husband, Anthony began attending the Avonlea school under Anne Shirley. From his very first day, he took a dislike to Anne, maintaining that female teachers were useless. He engaged in misbehavior, such as pouring water down Aurelia Clay's neck, but remained completely untouched by Anne's gentle reprimands and lectures on how gentlemen ought to behave. His attitude of contempt and mockery persisted, including an incident where he strutted impertinently and mocked her during a cold morning at school. He later placed a live mouse inside Anne's desk drawer, which led Anne to punish him physically until his bravado broke and he cried.

label: History
value: Aunt Jamesina was named after James.
unit: Aunt Jamesina was named after her father James, who drowned at sea a month prior to her birth. After her only daughter, Elizabeth, married and moved to India as a foreign missionary, Aunt Jamesina was left alone in a large house. She agreed to move to Kingsport to keep house for Anne Shirley, Stella, Priscilla, and Philippa Gordon at Patty's Place, bringing along her pet cat, the Sarah-cat. During her time keeping house at Patty's Place, she also adopted the cats Joseph and Rusty. Following the girls' graduation from Redmond College, she took the cats home with her and later set off to India to explore her daughter's mission field despite her intense fear of snakes.

She agreed to move to Kingsport to keep house for Anne Shirley, Stella, Priscilla, and Philippa Gordon at Patty's Place, bringing along her pet cat, the Sarah-cat. During her time keeping house at Patty's Place, she also adopted the cats Joseph and Rusty. Following the girls' graduation from Redmond College, she took the cats home with her and later set off to India to explore her daughter's mission field despite her intense fear of snakes.

label: History
value: At age twenty, Billy drove Anne Shirley to a concert at White Sands.
unit: At age twenty, Billy drove Anne Shirley, Jane Andrews, and Diana Barry to a concert at White Sands. Immensely admiring Anne, he proudly insisted she ride on the front seat with him, though his severe shyness caused him to slip away after the event to avoid attending the formal supper. After his father gave him the upper farm, Billy wished to marry Anne but was too shy to court her directly, compelling his sister Jane to ask for her hand on his behalf. Upon Anne's refusal, he did not break his heart and instead married Nettie Blewett. He proudly appeared in church with his new bride following Anne's return from college.

label: Appearance
value: Captain Jim was a tall man.
unit: Captain Jim was a tall, ungainly, and stooped man who possessed great strength and endurance. He had a homely, deeply lined, and bronzed face with spare jaws, a rugged mouth, a square brow, and a thick mane of iron-gray hair falling to his shoulders. His remarkably blue, deep-set eyes often twinkled or looked out seaward with a wistful, searching gaze. In his final spring, he appeared noticeably frailer, stooped, and grayer.

label: History
value: Captain Jim grew up on Prince Edward Island.
unit: Captain Jim grew up on Prince Edward Island, developing a passion for the sea inherited from his mother's side of the family. At sixteen, he formed a deep friendship with the Glen schoolmaster, John Selwyn, before running off to sea to spend five decades sailing to every corner of the globe. In his youth, he suffered a profound tragedy when his sweetheart, Margaret, died after drifting out to sea in a storm. He remained a bachelor for the rest of his life. After retiring from the sea, he became the keeper of the Four Winds Lighthouse. He rescued a injured, amnesiac Dick Moore in a Havana boarding house and brought him back to his wife Leslie. When Anne Shirley and Gilbert Blythe moved to Four Winds, Captain Jim quickly became one of their closest friends and a constant guest at their home. He shared his life-book of written memories with writer Owen Ford, collaborating with him to get his travels and life story published. Before his death, he rejoiced in the birth of Gilbert and Anne's son Little Jem, who was named in his honor. Following his death, his collection of world curiosities was bequeathed to Little Jem.

unit: Captain Jim grew up on Prince Edward Island, developing a passion for the sea inherited from his mother's side of the family. At sixteen, he formed a deep friendship with the Glen schoolmaster, John Selwyn, before running off to sea to spend five decades sailing to every corner of the globe. In his youth, he suffered a profound tragedy when his sweetheart, Margaret, died after drifting out to sea in a storm. He remained a bachelor for the rest of his life. After retiring from the sea, he became the keeper of the Four Winds Lighthouse. He rescued a injured, amnesiac Dick Moore in a Havana boarding house and brought him back to his wife Leslie. When Anne Shirley and Gilbert Blythe moved to Four Winds, Captain Jim quickly became one of their closest friends and a constant guest at their home. He shared his life-book of written memories with writer Owen Ford, collaborating with him to get his travels and life story published. Before his death, he rejoiced in the birth of Gilbert and Anne's son Little Jem, who was named in his honor. Following his death, his collection of world curiosities was bequeathed to Little Jem.

label: History
value: Carl lived in Maywater
unit: Carl lived in Maywater prior to moving to Glen St. Mary when his father was appointed minister of the Glen manse. Often spending time outdoors, he was frequently found studying ants or collecting small creatures like beetles, lizards, and toads. On one occasion, he caught a cellar snake using a forked stick, and on another, spent an afternoon watching an ant bed in the Methodist graveyard with Mary Vance. After getting wet while pursuing dragon-flies in the Rainbow Valley marsh, Carl suffered a severe sore throat and spent several days sick in bed, which contributed to his sisters confusing the days of the week. He co-founded the Good-Conduct Club with his siblings and friends on Hezekiah Pollock's tombstone. Later, Carl became dangerously ill with double pneumonia, but he rallied after a difficult night under the care of Dr. Blythe and a nurse. Following a misdeed that earned him a promised whipping from his father, Carl faced the punishment gamely to avoid adding to his father's regret.

On one occasion, he caught a cellar snake using a forked stick, and on another, spent an afternoon watching an ant bed in the Methodist graveyard with Mary Vance. After getting wet while pursuing dragon-flies in the Rainbow Valley marsh, Carl suffered a severe sore throat and spent several days sick in bed, which contributed to his sisters confusing the days of the week. He co-founded the Good-Conduct Club with his siblings and friends on Hezekiah Pollock's tombstone. Later, Carl became dangerously ill with double pneumonia, but he rallied after a difficult night under the care of Dr. Blythe and a nurse. Following a misdeed that earned him a promised whipping from his father, Carl faced the punishment gamely to avoid adding to his father's regret.

label: Quotes
value: > I’m real glad of that. They said I did at home, but I thought likely they just wanted to aggravate me. I don’t want no Yankee accent. Not that I’ve a word to say against the Yankees, Miss Shirley, ma’am. They’re real civilized. But give me old P.E. Island every time.

label: Quotes
value: > Goodness, no, Miss Shirley, ma’am. I wouldn’t know who he meant if he did. Of course, when we got married he had to say, 'I take thee, Leonora,’ and I declare to you, Miss Shirley, ma’am, I’ve had the most dreadful feeling ever since that it wasn’t me he was talking to and I haven’t been rightly married at all. And so you’re going to be married yourself, Miss Shirley, ma’am? I always thought I’d like to marry a doctor. It would be so handy when the children had measles and croup. Tom is only a bricklayer, but he’s real good-tempered. When I said to him, says I, 'Tom, can I go to Miss Shirley’s wedding? I mean to go anyhow, but I’d like to have your consent,’ he just says, 'Suit yourself, Charlotta, and you’ll suit me.’ That’s a real pleasant kind of husband to have, Miss Shirley, ma’am.

label: History
value: Charlotta came to live as a handmaiden at Echo Lodge
unit: Charlotta came to live as a handmaiden at Echo Lodge for Miss Lavendar Lewis at fourteen years of age, following her three older sisters who had worked there before her. She assisted Miss Lavendar faithfully with household tasks, gardening, and preparations for her mistress's wedding to Stephen Irving. Following the wedding, she moved to Boston with Mr. and Mrs. Irving, though she initially suffered from severe homesickness and preferred Prince Edward Island. During subsequent summers, she returned with the Irvings to Echo Lodge, having grown into a young lady. She later married an American bricklayer named Tom. She traveled back to the Island to attend Anne Shirley's wedding, enthusiastically throwing rice and old shoes as the newlyweds departed.

label: History
value: Cornelia Bryant grew up in Four Winds.
unit: Cornelia Bryant grew up in Four Winds as the daughter of Stephen Bryant. After her mother's death, she acted as mother and sister to her younger brother, whose early death in his twenties deeply grieved her. Despite receiving suitors in her youth, she remained unmarried for many years, earning a reputation as a sharp-tongued old maid with an underlying generosity toward anyone in trouble. When Anne Shirley and Gilbert Blythe moved to Four Winds, she quickly formed a close friendship with Anne and regularly visited them, frequently engaging in lighthearted debates with Captain Jim. She took a protective interest in Leslie Moore and helped look out for her well-being. Eventually, she accepted the marriage proposal of her long-time acquaintance Marshall Elliott and had been married to him for thirteen years by the time the Meredith family settled at the Glen St. Mary manse. Learning of the mistreatment of the orphan Mary Vance, Cornelia had her husband investigate and took the girl into her home to raise her, growing fond of her as a helpful companion.

label: History
value: Diana Barry grew up at Orchard Slope
unit: Diana Barry grew up at Orchard Slope and formed an immediate, lifelong bond of friendship with Anne Shirley when they met as children. She attended the Avonlea school, where she participated in school events, joined the childhood Story Club, and sang a solo at the concert. Though temporarily forbidden by her mother to play with Anne after accidentally drinking currant wine, Diana was reunited with her after Anne saved her sister Minnie May from croup. Diana chose not to attend Queen's Academy because her parents did not plan to send her to college, but she remained active in local life, serving as treasurer for the Avonlea Village Improvement Society. As she grew older, she entered a romance with Fred Wright, eventually getting married at Orchard Slope. In their early years of marriage, they settled into their new home and had two children, little Fred and Small Anne Cordelia.

label: History
value: Dick Moore grew up at the Glen.
unit: Dick Moore grew up at the Glen, where his father Abner kept a store. He became enamored with Leslie West, who repeatedly snubbed him, but he eventually coerced her into marriage with her mother's aid. After living with Leslie at the West place for a winter, he grew restless and went to Nova Scotia. From there, he joined his cousin George Moore on a voyage to Havana aboard the vessel Four Sisters. While in Cuba, Dick died of yellow fever thirteen years before his death became known to his community. For twelve years, his family and neighbors back at Four Winds mistook his injured and amnesiac cousin, George Moore, for Dick himself.

label: History
value: Ellen grew up living with Rosemary
unit: Ellen grew up living with her sister Rosemary and their mother after her father and brother died. In her youth, she went about with Norman Douglas for two years before a quarrel caused them to separate, leading Norman to marry someone else out of pique. Following her mother's death on Rosemary's twenty-fifth birthday, Ellen sank into a deep period of intense grief and melancholy. During this time, she had Rosemary swear a solemn vow over the Bible that neither of them would ever marry and that they would always live together. Over the years, she and Rosemary kept close to home, maintaining their household on the hill. Years later, Norman Douglas saw her at church and fell in love with her again, prompting him to pursue her and ultimately leading to their arrangement to marry.

label: History
value: Faith grew up in Maywater
unit: Faith grew up in Maywater before her family relocated to the manse in Glen St. Mary. Soon after arriving, she befriended the Ingleside children, forming a strong bond over a shared meal and setting up regular gatherings in Rainbow Valley. She frequently fell into scrapes due to her heedless nature, including accidentally dropping a pail of milk and eggs down the cellar and getting confused about days of the week, which led to her cleaning house on Sunday. When her pet rooster Adam was carved and served for supper by the visiting Rev. James Perry, Faith was deeply upset and detested the minister. In an attempt to solve the minister's salary issue, Faith impulsively visited Norman Douglas and convinced him to return to church, earning his respect and the nickname 'Red Rose'. Later, she helped form the Good-Conduct Club with her siblings to self-enforce discipline, though she suffered through punishments like eating soggy bread after mistaking a white object in the old Bailey garden for Henry Warren's ghost.

label: History
value: Gilbert lived in Alberta for three years
unit: After living in Alberta for three years with his ailing father, Gilbert returns to Avonlea to resume his schooling. He quickly establishes an intense academic rivalry with Anne Shirley. After attending Queen's Academy together, he selflessly surrenders his position at the Avonlea school to Anne so she can stay near Marilla, electing to teach at White Sands instead. He co-founds the Avonlea Village Improvement Society and acts as its president before entering Redmond College alongside Anne. During his freshman year at Redmond, he leads his class to victory in the Arts Rush, serves as Freshman Class president, and captains the football team. Gilbert eventually confesses his love to Anne, but she refuses his marriage proposal, after which he steps back to maintain a courteous distance. Following a grueling academic year in which he earns High Honors and the Cooper Prize, he falls critically ill with typhoid fever; upon learning that Anne is not engaged to Roy Gardner, he recovers rapidly and asks her again, winning her heart. After completing his medical studies, Gilbert marries Anne in the Green Gables orchard and moves to Four Winds Harbor to take over his great-uncle Dr. David Blythe's practice. He settles with Anne in a little house by the harbor, earns a reputation as a devoted physician by saving patients like Rhoda Allonby, and eventually plans a move into Glen St. Mary as his family and medical practice grow.

label: History
value: Mr. J. A. Harrison is originally from Scottsford, New Brunswick.
unit: Originally from Scottsford, New Brunswick, Mr. J. A. Harrison lived with his sister until her death, at which point he married Emily Scott to fulfill a deathbed promise. Following constant bickering over housekeeping habits and his profane parrot, Ginger, he separated from his wife and moved to Avonlea, buying the farm of Robert Bell. In Avonlea, he lived as a bachelor, hired John Henry Carter, and gained a local reputation as an outspoken crank. He initially clashed with Anne Shirley over a Jersey cow incident, but the two quickly became close friends and confidants, with Mr. Harrison offering her blunt feedback on her writing. After Ginger died, his wife Emily arrived in Avonlea and reconciled with him, after which he became a neat, regular churchgoer.

label: History
value: Jane grew up in Avonlea
unit: Jane grew up in Avonlea as part of the Harmon Andrews family. During her school days, she joined Anne Shirley, Diana Barry, and Ruby Gillis in forming a Story Club and taking part in Miss Stacy's recitations. After preparing for the Entrance examination, she attended Queen's Academy in the Second Class work and took top honors in the domestic science course. She began her career teaching in Newbridge, where her success placed her name on the Inspector's Roll of Honor, and she helped found the Avonlea Village Improvement Society. Later, after a period of teaching in Avonlea, she moved to the West to teach on the prairies. During a holiday break, she proposed to Anne Shirley on behalf of her shy brother Billy, though Anne declined. Upon returning from the West, she married Mr. Inglis, a Winnipeg millionaire, and took a wedding tour to Europe before settling into a happy life where her wealth did not spoil her sweet and sensible nature.

label: Personality
value: John Meredith is a deeply spiritual man.
unit: John Meredith is a deeply spiritual, shy, and aloof man who retains the heart of a boy. He is intensely absent-minded, frequently losing himself for days in theological studies or reading, often completely oblivious to his surroundings, meals, and parish duties. Despite his abstraction, he loves his children deeply and possesses a hidden, quiet sense of humor. He holds steadfast to his romantic ideals and high personal standards, refusing to marry merely out of common sense or parish necessity.

label: History
value: Cecilia died suddenly in Maywater.
unit: After the sudden death of his beloved wife Cecilia in Maywater, John Meredith became the Presbyterian minister at Glen St. Mary, living in the manse with his four children and Aunt Martha. Deeply immersed in his theological studies, he frequently neglected his daily surroundings, his parish duties, and the guidance of his children. While walking through Rainbow Valley, he formed a close, unreserved friendship with young Walter Blythe, and soon after met Rosemary West by the spring. Recognizing his deep feelings for Rosemary, he eventually proposed marriage to her, but was devastated when she sent him a cool letter of refusal. Stunned by parish criticism regarding his children's upbringing and terrified when his daughter Una fainted in church, he resolved to be a more attentive father despite his heartbreak over losing Rosemary.

Deeply immersed in his theological studies, he frequently neglected his daily surroundings, his parish duties, and the guidance of his children. While walking through Rainbow Valley, he formed a close, unreserved friendship with young Walter Blythe, and soon after met Rosemary West by the spring. Recognizing his deep feelings for Rosemary, he eventually proposed marriage to her, but was devastated when she sent him a cool letter of refusal. Stunned by parish criticism regarding his children's upbringing and terrified when his daughter Una fainted in church, he resolved to be a more attentive father despite his heartbreak over losing Rosemary.

label: History
value: During spelling class at Avonlea school, Josie cheated by looking in her book.
unit: During spelling class at Avonlea school, Josie cheated by looking in her book to get ahead, but got flustered when Anne Shirley caught her. During a outdoor gathering, Josie dared Jane Andrews to hop around the garden on one leg. When Jane failed, Josie celebrated her victory and was challenged in turn by Anne to walk along the top of the Barrys' board fence, which Josie accomplished with ease. When preparing for a concert, Josie became sulky because she wanted to play the fairy queen, a role given to Jane Andrews instead. Following the concert, she did not speak to Julia Bell for three months after commenting that Julia's bow resembled a chicken jerking its head. Upon seeing Anne's newly clipped hair, Josie remarked that she looked like a scarecrow. At the Exhibition, Josie earned first prize for her knitted lace. When studying for Queen's Academy Entrance exams, she reminded Anne that the number thirteen was unlucky. Later, while attending Queen's Academy, she earned a reputation as the sharpest-tongued student present. Unlike many of her classmates, she stated she planned to go to college for education's sake rather than out of necessity to earn a living. Later, when Anne's prize-winning story was published, Josie spitefully claimed Anne had merely copied it from an old paper.

During a outdoor gathering, Josie dared Jane Andrews to hop around the garden on one leg. When Jane failed, Josie celebrated her victory and was challenged in turn by Anne to walk along the top of the Barrys' board fence, which Josie accomplished with ease. When preparing for a concert, Josie became sulky because she wanted to play the fairy queen, a role given to Jane Andrews instead. Following the concert, she did not speak to Julia Bell for three months after commenting that Julia's bow resembled a chicken jerking its head. Upon seeing Anne's newly clipped hair, Josie remarked that she looked like a scarecrow. At the Exhibition, Josie earned first prize for her knitted lace. When studying for Queen's Academy Entrance exams, she reminded Anne that the number thirteen was unlucky. Later, while attending Queen's Academy, she earned a reputation as the sharpest-tongued student present. Unlike many of her classmates, she stated she planned to go to college for education's sake rather than out of necessity to earn a living. Later, when Anne's prize-winning story was published, Josie spitefully claimed Anne had merely copied it from an old paper.

label: Personality
value: Lavendar Lewis is an imaginative woman.
unit: She is an imaginative, romantic, and warm-hearted woman who maintains the youthfulness of her heart. Despite a lonely life, she is generally a happy and contented person who enjoys life's simple pleasures, tea parties, and play-pretend. By her own admission, she can be sulky and proud when hurt. She is deeply hospitable and forms strong, affectionate friendships.

label: History
value: After her mother died, Lavendar lived at Echo Lodge in Grafton.
unit: After her mother died, Lavendar lived at Echo Lodge in Grafton and hired Charlotta Bowman to stay with her for board and clothes, continuing to hire her sisters under the name Charlotta. Anne Shirley and Diana Barry discovered her secluded home and established a close friendship with her, joining in her imaginative tea parties and cozy gatherings. When Anne introduced Stephen Irving's young son Paul to her, Paul wrote to his father about her, prompting Stephen to return to Grafton after twenty-five years. Stephen and Lavendar reconciled their past misunderstandings, rekindled their romance, and were married in her honeysuckle arbor at Echo Lodge. Following their wedding, they moved west to the Pacific coast. Years later, she returned with Stephen and Paul to visit Echo Lodge and her friends in Avonlea.

When Anne introduced Stephen Irving's young son Paul to her, Paul wrote to his father about her, prompting Stephen to return to Grafton after twenty-five years. Stephen and Lavendar reconciled their past misunderstandings, rekindled their romance, and were married in her honeysuckle arbor at Echo Lodge. Following their wedding, they moved west to the Pacific coast. Years later, she returned with Stephen and Paul to visit Echo Lodge and her friends in Avonlea.

label: History
value: Leslie grew up in Four Winds.
unit: Leslie grew up in Four Winds as the adored daughter of Frank West. After witnessing her brother's tragic death and discovering her father's suicide, she resolved to work her way through Queen's Academy and teach. At sixteen, she was coerced into marrying Dick Moore to prevent her mother's home from being mortgaged away. Shortly after her mother's death, Dick went off to sea, only to be brought back years later as an invalid with no memory or intellect. Leslie spent eleven long years loyally nursing him at her old family farm while living in extreme poverty and isolation. Her life changed after befriending Anne Shirley and Gilbert Blythe, whose circle introduced her to new hope and joy. Encouraged by Gilbert to seek medical help, Leslie took Dick to Montreal for surgery, where it was discovered that the man was actually Dick's cousin, George Moore, leaving Leslie legally free. She later fell in love with writer Owen Ford and accepted his proposal in Anne's garden.

After witnessing her brother's tragic death and discovering her father's suicide, she resolved to work her way through Queen's Academy and teach. At sixteen, she was coerced into marrying Dick Moore to prevent her mother's home from being mortgaged away. Shortly after her mother's death, Dick went off to sea, only to be brought back years later as an invalid with no memory or intellect. Leslie spent eleven long years loyally nursing him at her old family farm while living in extreme poverty and isolation. Her life changed after befriending Anne Shirley and Gilbert Blythe, whose circle introduced her to new hope and joy. Encouraged by Gilbert to seek medical help, Leslie took Dick to Montreal for surgery, where it was discovered that the man was actually Dick's cousin, George Moore, leaving Leslie legally free. She later fell in love with writer Owen Ford and accepted his proposal in Anne's garden.

label: History
value: Jem was born at the little house of dreams.
unit: Jem was born at the little house of dreams by the harbour shore, the firstborn child of Anne Shirley and Gilbert Blythe. During his babyhood, Captain Jim Boyd bequeathed him a collection of curios. As he grew up at Ingleside, he became known for his extensive firsthand knowledge of nature and his propensity to test statements experimentally. He maintained a standing feud with the housekeeper Susan over her nickname for him, 'Little Jem'. During his childhood, he frequented Rainbow Valley alongside his siblings and friends, showing special affection for his mother by picking her wild flowers like mayflowers and arbutus. He played games like quoits with Jerry Corcoran and was regarded as the squarest boy in Glen St. Mary, leading to his selection as umpire for the Good-Conduct Club. As he approached age fourteen, he spent his evenings studying in the Ingleside garret for the entrance examination to Queen's Academy. After a final gathering in Rainbow Valley with his companions, he prepared to leave for Charlottetown to attend the academy.

Despite her restrained emotional expression, she cares fiercely for those she loves and is capable of deep warmth.

label: History
value: Marilla Cuthbert lived her entire life at Green Gables.
unit: Marilla Cuthbert lived her entire life at Green Gables in Avonlea alongside her unmarried brother Matthew. When they intended to adopt a young boy from an asylum to help on the farm, a mistake resulted in the arrival of Anne Shirley. Although initially hesitant, Marilla resolved to keep and raise Anne, gradually coming to love the wild, imaginative child deeply. After Matthew's sudden death from heart failure, Marilla decided to keep Green Gables with Anne's help. Following the death of a distant relative, she took in six-year-old twins, Davy and Dora Keith, taking charge of their upbringing. In her later years, she traveled away from Avonlea for the first time to visit Anne in Four Winds for Christmas and later returned to assist Anne after the birth of her children. Marilla spends her old age at Green Gables enjoying visits from Anne's children, particularly favoring Anne's eldest son, Jem.

unit: Marilla Cuthbert lived her entire life at Green Gables in Avonlea alongside her unmarried brother Matthew. label: History
value: Marshall Elliott was born a passionate Liberal Grit.
unit: Born a passionate Liberal Grit, Marshall Elliott swore at a public political meeting during a bitter election campaign that he would not cut his hair or shave his beard until the Grits returned to power. He kept his word for fifteen years, becoming a well-known local eccentric who frequently fished with Captain Jim. One New Year's Eve, he visited the lighthouse, sang ballads, and danced gracefully with Leslie Moore. When the Liberals finally won the election years later, he quietly walked out of the store on receiving the news at midnight and went straight to Augustus Palmer's barber shop to be shaved and trimmed. Shortly after his hair was cut, he married Cornelia Bryant, remaining happily wed to her for over thirteen years. On one occasion, he investigated rumors of child abuse over-harbour on Cornelia's behalf and was infuriated to learn how severely young Mary had been mistreated by Mrs. Wiley.

label: History
value: Mary Vance ran away from Mrs. Wiley
unit: After running away from the abusive Mrs. Wiley, Mary Vance was found starving in James Taylor's old hay barn by the Meredith children, who took her in and befriended her. She quickly joined the circle of children in Rainbow Valley, sharing new games, shadow pictures, and ghost stories. When Rilla Blythe angered her, Mary chased and terrified her with a dried codfish, but she later felt repentant for her behavior. Following Mrs. Wiley's death, Miss Cornelia Elliott took Mary into her home to raise her, work her into shape, and teach her religious instruction. Under Miss Cornelia's care, Mary flourished into a plump, well-dressed, and exceptionally hard worker. She continued to hang around Rainbow Valley as a lively companion, frequently lecturing the Merediths and warning them against the dangers of stepmothers.

unit: After running away from the abusive Mrs. Wiley, Mary Vance was found starving in James Taylor's old hay barn by the Meredith children, who took her in and befriended her. She quickly joined the circle of children in Rainbow Valley, sharing new games, shadow pictures, and ghost stories. When Rilla Blythe angered her, Mary chased and terrified her with a dried codfish, but she later felt repentant for her behavior. Following Mrs. Wiley's death, Miss Cornelia Elliott took Mary into her home to raise her, work her into shape, and teach her religious instruction. Under Miss Cornelia's care, Mary flourished into a plump, well-dressed, and exceptionally hard worker. She continued to hang around Rainbow Valley as a lively companion, frequently lecturing the Merediths and warning them against the dangers of stepmothers.

label: History
value: Matthew Cuthbert worked the family farm at Green Gables.
unit: Matthew Cuthbert spent his life working the family farm at Green Gables alongside his sister Marilla. Due to his advancing age and failing heart, the siblings arranged to adopt an orphan boy to assist with farm work, but Matthew was sent to Bright River station and accidentally brought back Anne Shirley instead. Despite his lifelong dread of women and children, he immediately took a liking to Anne and quietly persuaded Marilla to keep her. Over the following years, Matthew served as Anne's gentle champion, secretly buying her a fashionable puff-sleeved dress for a school concert and encouraging her romantic spirit. He suffered worsening heart spells and eventually died instantaneously on the porch of Green Gables after reading news of the Abbey Bank's failure. Following his death, Anne maintained a lifelong reverence for his memory, regularly visiting his grave.

label: History
value: Norman Douglas courted Ellen West
unit: In his youth, Norman Douglas courted Ellen West for two years before a quarrel led to their separation. In a fit of temper, Norman married Hester Reese to spite Ellen, but he despised Hester's meekness and broke what little spirit she had. After a dispute over a cow deal with a church session member, he refused to attend church for twenty years. Ten years after burying his wife, Norman was visited by Faith Meredith, whose spirited temper during a disagreement over church attendance earned his respect and convinced him to return to church services. Upon returning to church, he saw Ellen West again and fell in love with her once more. He began attending social gatherings and courting Ellen publicly, engaging in persistent bullying and coaxing until they agreed to marry.

label: History
value: Owen Ford traveled to Four Winds.
unit: Owen Ford traveled to Four Winds to recover from typhoid fever on his doctor's advice and to see his grandparents' old home. While staying in Four Winds, he befriended Anne and Gilbert Blythe and fell deeply in love with Leslie Moore. Recognizing the rich potential in Captain Jim Boyd's life experiences, Owen collaborated with him to write a book based on Captain Jim's life. He temporarily left Four Winds after confessing his feelings for Leslie to Anne, but returned after Leslie was free to court her. Owen and Leslie married, had children, and later set off on a year-long trip to Japan so Owen could gather material for his next novel.

label: History
value: Paul Irving came from Boston to Avonlea
unit: Paul Irving came from Boston to Avonlea to live with his grandmother on the shore road after the death of his mother. At the Avonlea school, he quickly formed a deep bond with his teacher, Anne Shirley, who recognized his poetic genius and became his close confidante. As a child, he fought a drawn battle with schoolmate St. Clair Donnell to defend the American flag and nurtured childhood crushes while enjoying imaginative stories about "rock people" and "dream-people." He later met Miss Lavendar Lewis, who eventually married his father, Stephen Irving, giving Paul a loving stepmother whom he called "Mother Lavendar." After his father and stepmother relocated to Boston, Paul eventually joined them, growing into a tall young man interested in football and literature. He successfully published a volume of poetry and drove the carriage for Anne and Gilbert Blythe on their wedding day. Later, he embarked on a two-year period of study abroad in Europe, remaining an inspirational model of poetry for Anne's son Walter.

label: History
value: Philippa Gordon attended Redmond College.
unit: Philippa Gordon attended Redmond College, where her background, beauty, and charm opened doors to social circles, allowing her to introduce her new friends Anne Shirley and Priscilla Grant to college life. She competed closely with Anne and Gilbert Blythe for leadership in Freshman classes while simultaneously torn between two hometown suitors, Alec and Alonzo. Before her second year, she joined Anne, Priscilla, and Stella Maynard in renting Patty's Place under the chaperonage of Aunt Jamesina. While spending time at Prospect Point, she met Jonas Blake, a minister and fellow Redmond graduate, and fell deeply in love with him. Determined to prove her cleverness to Jonas, she aimed for the Johnson Scholarship in Mathematics and accepted his proposal of marriage. Despite initial disapproval from her mother, she held firm to her engagement, completed her studies at Redmond, and married Jonas in Bolingbroke with Anne serving as her bridesmaid. Later, she wrote to Gilbert Blythe to inform him that Anne was not engaged to Roy Gardner, encouraging him to try again.

value: Mr. Phillips served as the schoolmaster in Avonlea.
unit: Mr. Phillips served as the schoolmaster in Avonlea. During his tenure, he was noted for keeping poor order in the classroom, constantly resorting to whipping his pupils without gaining their respect or discipline. He focused most of his time and attention on the older scholars preparing for Queen's College, while neglecting the younger students and paying special attention to Prissy Andrews. He held up Anne Shirley's slate to humiliate her before the class on her first day of school, and later punished her by making her stand on the platform. After whipping Sam Boulter for talking back in class, Sam's father came to the school to confront him. Despite his incompetence as a teacher, he retained his position for another year because his uncle was an influential school trustee.

He focused most of his time and attention on the older scholars preparing for Queen's College, while neglecting the younger students and paying special attention to Prissy Andrews. He held up Anne Shirley's slate to humiliate her before the class on her first day of school, and later punished her by making her stand on the platform. After whipping Sam Boulter for talking back in class, Sam's father came to the school to confront him. Despite his incompetence as a teacher, he retained his position for another year because his uncle was an influential school trustee.

value: Priscilla studied at Queen's Academy.
unit: Priscilla studied at Queen's Academy, where she formed a close circle of intimate friends with Anne Shirley and Stella Maynard. After graduating, she prepared to teach at her home school and participated in the Avonlea Village Improvement Society, for which she wrote a paper on cemeteries. Later, she gained her father's consent to attend Redmond College in Kingsport, boarding and studying classics alongside Anne Shirley, Philippa Gordon, and Stella Maynard at Patty's Place. After finishing her studies at Redmond, Priscilla married a handsome foreign missionary who praised her beauty, and the couple subsequently moved to Japan.

label: Personality
value: Mrs. Rachel is a capable woman.
unit: Mrs. Rachel is a capable, outspoken, and farseeing woman who prides herself on speaking her mind without fear or favor. Although officious, opinionated, and given to bossing and nagging others to do right, she possesses a warm, good, and kindly heart. She is deeply devoted to church affairs, strict in her standards of modesty and propriety, and a passionate politician. A shrewd observer of human nature, she believes firmly in foreordination and predestination.

label: History
value: Jonas Blake was a theological student
unit: Jonas Blake was a theological student from St. Columbia who took charge of the Point Prospect Mission Church for a summer. During this time, he became good chums with Philippa Gordon, spending time fishing, boating, and walking with her. Although he resisted becoming a minister for a long time, he ultimately embraced the calling. He frequently visited Patty's Place while taking early and late trains from St. Columbia, becoming popular among the residents. After proposing to Philippa Gordon, he met her parents at Mount Holly and gained their affection despite her mother's initial opposition. The two were married the following June. Years later, he attended Anne Shirley and Gilbert Blythe's wedding with Philippa, delivering a beautiful wedding prayer during the ceremony.

label: History
value: Roy Gardner belonged to an elite Kingsport family.
unit: Roy Gardner belonged to an elite Kingsport family, but was forced to interrupt his college studies for two years to travel abroad with his ailing mother. After returning to Redmond, he met Anne Shirley and began courting her in a lavishly romantic manner, frequently sending her orchids, violets, and sonnets. His attentiveness made him a frequent topic of gossip and social expectation among college social circles. Over time, his mother and sisters came to welcome Anne into their circle. Eventually, Roy proposed marriage to Anne, but she declined his proposal after realizing she did not love him.

label: History
value: Ruby grew up in Avonlea.
unit: Ruby grew up in Avonlea among a large family of sisters. In her schooldays at Avonlea School, she was part of the local girl circle, joining Anne Shirley, Diana Barry, and Jane Andrews in school dialogues, concerts, and their creative Story Club. She later studied for the Entrance exams alongside her classmates and attended Queen's Academy to earn a teaching certificate. Upon completing her studies, she took a position as the schoolteacher at Carmody, though her primary focus remained on her numerous admirers and romantic prospects. During a visit to Boston, she began suffering health complications and contracted galloping consumption, forcing her to give up teaching in the winter. Despite her failing health, she remained hopeful about securing the White Sands school in the fall. She passed away peacefully in her sleep at her home in Avonlea.

Her term at Avonlea school ended in June, though she later returned to the area for visits and social occasions.

unit: Una is a dreamy, sweet, and timid girl who is deeply sensitive to public opinion. She is gentle, polite, compassionate, and tender-hearted, hating fighting and crying out of sympathy for others. Unlike most of her peers, she genuinely enjoys praying and is pious. Although shy and easily quailing at daunting tasks, she possesses a selfless devotion to her family, especially her father.

label: History
value: Una grew up in Maywater.
unit: Una grew up in Maywater before moving with her minister father and siblings to Glen St. Mary. After befriending the Ingleside children, she helped harbor the runaway orphan Mary Vance, who taught her how to wash dishes and shared terrifying stories that shaped Una's fear of ghosts and stepmothers. When Mrs. Alec Davis attempted to adopt Una from her father, Mr. Meredith was shaken into realizing his neglect of his children. Later, during a strict self-imposed fast for the Good-Conduct Club, Una fainted during a church service, alarming her father and Dr. Gilbert Blythe. After hearing her father privately voice his anguish over his love for Rosemary West, Una bravely conquered her shyness and walked to Rosemary's house to ask her to marry her father to make him happy. Rosemary reassured Una that she would be a friend rather than a cruel stepmother.

value: Walter possesses a vivid imagination.

Sensitive and empathetic, he tends to take the blame on himself, while strongly disliking physical pain, ugly things, and seeing others get hurt.

label: History
value: Walter grew up at Ingleside.
unit: Walter grew up at Ingleside as one of the Blythe children, frequently spending his evenings reading aloud or playing with his siblings and friends in Rainbow Valley. Despite being considered soft or timid by fellow students at Glen St. Mary school due to his dislike of sports and fighting, he earned respect for his eloquent way of talking. He spent much of his time writing secret poetry and an epic, sharing his writings exclusively with his sister Di. After Dan Reese insulted both Walter's mother and Faith Meredith, Walter overcame his deep-seated horror of violence and fought Dan after school, gaining the victory. Following the fight, Walter declared he would no longer be afraid of things and resolved to have his aching tooth pulled.
